chunks: And from him, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Ja'far ibn Bashir, from Hammad, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Zurarah, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:

He asked: 'What is the distance between you and the grave of Husayn (peace be upon him)?' I replied: 'Sixteen or seventeen parasangs.' He asked: 'Do you not go to him?' I replied: 'No.' He said: 'How negligent you are!'

key_terms.أَجْفَاكُمْ: How negligent you are / How far you are from the truth
key_terms.فَرْسَخ: A parasang, an ancient unit of distance
key_terms.قَبْرُ الْحُسَيْنِ: The grave of Imam Husayn (peace be upon him)

ai.seo_question: What did Imam al-Baqir say about the neglect of visiting the grave of Imam Husayn?
ai.summary: Imam al-Baqir (a.s.) uses the rhetorical question 'What has alienated you?' to highlight the spiritual paradox of physical proximity versus spiritual neglect, a key theme in Shia devotional practice. This narration underscores the concept of *Jafa* (alienation) not as geographical distance, but as a failure of the heart to connect with the Ahl al-Bayt, emphasizing that the ease of access to Imam Husayn’s shrine should inspire greater devotion rather than complacency.

en.sayyid-mohsen-al-husayni-al-milani: 7. Muḥammad ibn Ja’far narrated to me from Muḥammad ibn Ḥusain, from Ja’far ibn Bashīr, from Ḥammād, from Muḥammad ibn Muslim, from Zurārah, who said: Abū Ja’far (Imam Bāqir (a.s.))

asked, “What is the distance between you and the grave of Ḥusain (a.s.)?” I replied, “Sixteen or seventeen parasangs.” Imam (a.s.) asked, “Do you not go to him?” I replied, “No.” Imam (a.s.) said, “How negligent you (people) are!!!”
